description.narrative: Making food systems resource efficient, environmentally sustainable, and resilient to shocks is an opportunity for agricultural transformation, sustainable economic diversification and to minimize greenhouse gas emissions. Sustainable food systems are crucial to ensure food security in all its dimensions and should take into account nutrition and food safety issues. Adopting a food systems approach to agrifood policies and investments makes it possible to seek economic, environmental, and social sustainability simultaneously.To achieve this goal, an important role is played by the availability of accurate, timely and accessible agricultural data and statistics. Lack of access to data and limited transparency in production hinder policy making and policy evaluation processes. As mentioned before, to achieve a successful agricultural transformation, developing countries need to foster an evidencebased approach to policy making that results in making public action both transparent and measurable in its impact through strategic use of statistics. At present, many countries, in particular in Sub Saharan Africa (SSA), lack national monitoring and evaluation framework for agriculture that can enable policy makers to prioritize policies based on evidence, collect relevant data and monitor and evaluate their impact. The 50x2030 Initiative and the Agriculture and Food Global Practice (AGF) of the World Bank share a common vision to improve the state of agricultural data and statistics in SSA, particularly as relevant to the agricultural transformation, leveraging countrylevel investments in collecting and utilizing such data and exploiting synergies in their work programs towards these shared objectives. Data and statistics are also essential for the digital transformation of the agriculture sector as they present an opportunity to gather data which are foundational to the development and implementation of new data driven policy designs and of digital solutions in agriculture enabling the more efficient delivery of public and private digital services. Developments in the data and digital space highlight how data can be further reused, providing opportunities for data to serve multiple objectives. This includes for example the development and implementation of new policy designs and for the development of more efficient public and private agriculture services. The capacity to reuse such foundational data, not only for the better understanding of the agriculture sector in a country, but for more efficient policy designs and make insights more easily actionable including through the provision of new types of public services can unleash the opportunities offered by the digital technologies to transform agriculture and food system.
